title: Asia's data center boom hits speed bumps
key_facts: Australian neocloud firm Firmus (backed by Blackstone, Jane Street and Nvidia) withdrew its planned AU$7.1 billion (US$4.97 billion) ASX listing on Friday 9 Oct 2026 and, per the Financial Times, will seek up to $3 billion in private funds.
It had struggled to win market support at about AU$11 a share, and even after offering a cut, investors did not have the appetite.
Trading in Maas Group, a Firmus shareholder with a 3.2% stake, was halted after its shares fell 27% in two days.
Philippine telecoms firm PLDT put the listing of its data centre property trust Vitro on hold until 2027, citing 'current market conditions and rising interest rates'.
Indonesia's West Java province halted a 640 MW project by Singapore-based BDX last week for lacking key approvals including an environmental assessment.
A month ago Thailand suspended 166 data centre projects, 49 under construction and 117 awaiting approval, to write new rules.
Malaysia's Energy Commission head Siti Safinah Salleh is reported to have said electricity demand growth went from 1.5%-2% a year to nearly 10% due to data centres.
quote_evidence: Asia-Pacific's hectic data center rollout has hit a series of speed bumps.
PLDT said in an exchange filing it had decided to delay the IPO until 2027 due to "current market conditions and rising interest rates."
why_it_matters_hint: Funding and government approvals are slowing Asia's data centre build-out.
event_date: Fri 9 Oct 2026 (Firmus); other events over the past month
notes: Roundup piece. Light Reading says CDC dumped Firmus 'two days earlier'; our 6 Oct edition carried that split from Rampart, so the timing was not repeated.
